summary: You can finish with no subplan or pick History and Philosophy of Science (61 units) or Philosophy and Literary Thought (65 units). With no subplan, the audit checks an introductory course, the five breadth areas (logic, both history of philosophy courses PHIL 100 and PHIL 102, contemporary theoretical philosophy, philosophy of science, and moral and political philosophy, each for at least 3 units with a C- or better), Philosophy electives with at least 9 units numbered 99 and above, PHIL 80 for WIM (a separate course from the introductory one) and a PHIL 194 capstone, 60 units in all, with honors courses PHIL 196-199 adding none. Each subplan has its own required courses and unit total. At most 10 units graded S or CR count, and PHIL 196-199 do not count toward a subplan's units. Checked by hand: courses without a Bulletin list (science, history of science, national literature, and the subplan depth and capstone courses), which you move in, and at most two transfer courses for 10 units. Honors is optional.
